title: AI-POWERED OFFICIAL LANGUAGES LEARNING SOLUTION
description: The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) is exploring tools to support employees in learning their second official language (English or French) in response to evolving operational and legislative requirements. The modernization of the Official Languages Act has reinforced the importance of maintaining and strengthening bilingual capacity across the organization to ensure compliance with the Agency's obligations to serve Canadians and support employees in the official language of their choice. Investing in effective and accessible second-language learning solutions will help the CRA maintain its bilingual capacity, support succession planning, and continue providing high-quality services in both official languages. As a result, the CRA is assessing the feasibility of implementing a scalable, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered language learning solution aligned with CRA corporate requirements and Government of Canada requirements. Responding to this Request for Information (RFI) is not a prerequisite to being eligible to bid on any subsequent solicitation. Any subsequent solicitation will be advertised on the Government Electronic Tendering Service commonly referred to as CanadaBuys. This RFI is not to be construed as a solicitation for tenders or proposals. No contract or other form of commitment will be entered into based on responses to this RFI. This RFI is not authorization by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) to undertake any work that would result in costs to the CRA. RFI Closing Date Responses must be received on or before October 22, 2026, no later than 14:00 EDT. All responses to this Request for Information must be directed in writing and submitted by email to: Contracting Authority: Charles Safarian E-mail: charles.safarian@cra-arc.gc.ca It is recommended that all electronic submissions contain a read receipt option to confirm that the email was received. Respondents are requested to provide a contact name, email address and telephone number when submitting their response. Please refer to the solicitation documents for further information and instructions regarding this opportunity.

title: Rental of equipment, machinery and tools
description: Description of Requirement: Canadian Heritage (PCH) is seeking the services of Offerors who can fulfil the rental of equipment, machinery and tools for such events. PCH Capital Experience Branch, as part of its mandate, produces major events which include Canada Day, Winterlude, Winter Lights Across Canada and other events annually. To support these productions and all its operations, PCH requires different types of equipment, machinery, and tools from time to time on an as-and-when-required basis. Evaluation Process and Selection Methodology: All offers will be evaluated to determine if the Mandatory Technical Criteria detailed in Attachment 1 to Part 4 of the RFSO have been met. Offers that do not meet ALL Mandatory Technical Criteria will be declared non-responsive and their Offer will be given no further consideration. Basis of Selection – Mandatory Technical Criteria Only: An offer must comply with the requirements of the Request for Standing Offers and meet all mandatory technical evaluation criteria to be declared responsive. The responsive offer(s) with the lowest evaluated price will be recommended for issuance of a Standing Offer. Security Requirements: During the term of the Standing Offer, including the option year, should the Offeror’s personnel require access to sensitive work sites such as Parliament Hill, PCH will inform the Offeror and its personnel and PCH will grant or approve their SITE ACCESS CLEARANCE.

title: Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT Canada has a requirement for the item detailed below: GSIN: N1375 – Demolition Materials UNSPSC: 46101600 –Ammunition Description: Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 A requirement exists to resupply Canada with the Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7. The Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 is required as the first step of an explosive shockwave in an explosive train when using a non-electric method of initiation. It is functioned by inserting an igniferous burning fuse into the open end and being crimped onto the burning fuse. When the flame from the burning fuse exits the end of the fuse, it ignites a primary explosive composition which in turn transfers a shockwave into the secondary explosive component in the Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7. The Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 is primarily used in military applications for demolition purposes. Quantity: 3,000 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Dundurn, Dundurn, Saskatchewan on or before 01 November 2027. 3,500 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Angus, Angus, Ontario on or before 01 November 2027. 3,000 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Dundurn, Dundurn, Saskatchewan between 01 September 2028 and 30 November 2028. 3,500 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Angus, Angus, Ontario between 01 September 2028 and 30 November 2028. description: This solicitation will be designated as a 100% Small Business set aside. A single award acquisition will be made. The awardee must be Small Business certified at time of award. This procurement is conducted under Far subpart 36.102, which requires A-E contracts to be negotiated on the basis of demonstrated competence and qualifications for the required professional services. A Standard Form (SF) 330 will be required. This project includes Design Phase architecture and engineering (A&E) services for Project AFBCIF# 270022 (Project #ZQEL 25-0004), Repair Club Kitchen and Dining Room at Youngstown ARS. Scope of work includes technical engineering specifications, structural drawings, and floor layouts through 35%, 65%, and 100% design completion marks. The project site is located at the 910 Airlift Wing (AFRC), Youngstown Air Reserve Station, 3976 King Graves Rd, Vienna OH 44473-5931 (Trumbull County). The magnitude of this project is between $100,000 and $250,000. Total contract performance period is 120 calendar days from the date of receipt of the notice to proceed. The award will be a Firm-Fixed Price contract. The NAICS Code is 541310; the Size Standard is $12.5 million average annual receipts over the past three years. Paper copies of the solicitation will not be provided as these documents, which include the solicitation and specifications, can be downloaded from https://sam.gov and should be available on or about 24 September 2026. As this is a federal construction project, the Construction Wage Rate Requirement applies. Once the solicitation is posted, it is incumbent upon the interested parties to review this posting frequently for any updates, changes, and/or amendments to any and all documents. The closing date for submission of offers is estimated to be on or about 22 October 2026 at 10:00am EDT and will be contained in the solicitation package. Interested parties should identify themselves by registering on the Interested Vendors List (IVL) found on the sam.gov website. Contractors are advised that in order to receive an award as the prime contractor, they must be listed and active in the System for Award Management (SAM) database for the NAICS code 541310. Failure to register will disqualify a contractor from award should the contractor be selected, not registered, nor active at the time of submission. Contractors may register via the Internet SAM website at https://sam.gov. Recommend registering immediately in order to be eligible for timely award. Contractors are also advised that they must complete the Online Representations and Certifications Application or risk having their proposals declared non-responsive. All responsible sources may submit a SF 330 which shall be considered by the Air Force Reserves. The dates cited above are estimates, not actual.

description: 9/17/2026- Amendment 001 Posted 8/3/2026- Replaces word versions of Attachements C04c_2a, C04d_3a and C04e_4a (Appendicies A-C) with PDFs. No other corrections. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Proposals are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26R4014 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the Bitterroot Front G-Z Long Term Integrated Resource Service Contract. The Bitterroot Front Project area spans roughly 145,000 acres across the Stevensville and Darby Ranger Districts, where dense, overstocked mixed?conifer stands and widespread tree mortality have increased susceptibility to insect outbreaks and extreme wildfire behavior. Following a decade of severe fires, the project aims to reduce wildfire risk to nearby communities and restore forest health through treatments such as thinning, harvesting, mechanical fuel reduction, and prescribed burning. These efforts focus on improving stand vigor, promoting fire?adapted species, reducing hazardous fuels, and enhancing safety and effectiveness for wildfire responders. A secondary objective of the long?term contract is to provide a consistent timber supply for local forest products industries, while contractors complete tasks including unit layout, timber cruising, road work, and timber removal as part of a broader strategy to increase the pace and scale of forest restoration. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 113310 and the small business size standard is 500 Employees This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. Proposals are to be submitted via email to Mark Phillipp at mark.phillipp@usda.gov and Matt Daigle at matthew.daigle@usda.gov.

description: This requirement is for the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. Shield Specialize Emergency Services Inc. Veolia es Canada Services Industriels Inc. Miller Environmental SUMAS Environmental Services Quest Disposal & Recycling Environmental 360 Solutions Description of the Requirement: Lead Hazardous Waste Removal for RCMP Indoor Firing Ranges (IFR), Alberta The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) K Division, Real Property and Asset Management has a requirement for the cleaning, removal, packing, disposal and/or recycling of hazardous waste materials from four RCMP Indoor Firing ranges located in Edmonton, Red Deer, Edson and St. Paul, Alberta. Level of Security Requirement: Resource Minimum Security Level Required: RCMP Facility Access Level 2 with Escort (FA2) Applicable Trade Agreements: Canada Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Columbia Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement, Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement, Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), and World Trade Organization – Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP) Proposed period of contract: The proposed period of contract shall be for one year from date of contract award inclusive, with the irrevocable option to extend the term of the Contract by up to three additional one year periods under the same conditions. Estimated Level of Effort: The estimated level of effort of the contract, per year and across all 4 locations, will be: 10 times per year : Using steel rod, check the depth of rubber pellets from surface of trap to rigid steps of the bullet trap structure or new lead buildup in the middle of trap and its both corners. Add rubber pellets into bullet trap to maintain 600mm (24 inches) depth. Refill the trap hopper with new rubber pellets. Rake rubber pellets to cover rubber membrane at the back of the trap with rubber pellets. Level rubber berm surface to make proper slope. 5 times per year: Fix, patch, and/or flip rubber curtains if applicable 4 times per year: Replacement of rubber curtains or panels if applicable 4 times per year: Lead mining of the bullet trap system 4 times per year: Deep cleaning of firing range, range walls 1.8m AFF, training gear (e.g., target holders, First Air kit, etc.), all horizontal surfaces, control and gun cleaning rooms, floors, HEPA vacuum inside filter sections of supply and exhaust units 5 times per year: Replacement of pre-filters for exhaust ventilation unit HEPA filters replacement must be coordinated with Project Authority and to be done every 5 years (for Edson, St. Paul, and Red Deer sites), and every 4 years (Edmonton HQ) The estimated level of effort provided is for bid evaluated price determination purposes only. Their inclusion does not represent a commitment by Canada that Canada’s future usage of the services described in the bid solicitation will be consistent with this data. title: Ireland – Social research services – Request for Tenders for the Provision of a Rapid Evidence Assessment in relation to reading for pleasure among children and young people in Ireland with a particular focus on boys and young men
description: The Department of Education and Youth is seeking research services from a suitably qualified contractor/s to conduct a rapid evidence review in relation to reading for pleasure among children and young people in Ireland, with a particular focus on boys and young men. For the purposes of this review, the terms children and young people and boys and young men refer to learners from the early learning and care (ELC) sector through primary and post-primary education. The review should therefore consider evidence relating to attitudes, engagement and participation in reading for pleasure across the continuum of educational provision, including key developmental and educational transition points.

title: Ireland – Social research services – Request for Tender for the provision of a rapid evidence review in relation to confidence in maths among children and young people in Ireland with a particular focus on girls and young women
description: The Department is seeking research services from a suitably qualified contractor(s) to conduct a rapid evidence review in relation to confidence in mathematics among children and young people in Ireland, with a particular focus on girls and young women. For the purposes of this review, the terms children and young people and girls and young women refer to learners from the early learning and care (ELC) sector through primary and post-primary education. The review should therefore consider evidence relating to confidence in mathematics and numeracy, including learners' self-belief, mathematical self-efficacy, attitudes towards mathematics, and willingness to engage with mathematical learning across the continuum of educational provision, including key developmental and educational transition points.

BACKGROUND AND SCOPE The United States (US) Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance & Special Operations Forces (ISR & SOF) Directorate, Special Warfare (SW) Program Office (AFLCMC/WISN) is conducting market research to identify possible sources capable of providing the NGOCS. CAPABILITY GAP Operators currently lack a lightweight, ruggedized, modular body-worn power, data, and edge-compute architecture capable of providing distributed processing capacity beyond the End User Device (EUD) for concurrent high-demand tactical workloads. Fielded systems rely on aging architecture, proprietary cabling, and limited processing capabilities at the edge. Consequently, the EUD is forced to absorb the entirety of application processing, edge-server hosting, message routing, video data links, and peripheral management. During high-tempo combat operations, this overreliance creates latency, power depletion, and reliability bottlenecks that can jeopardize the mission. title: Coburn Gore LPOE Art in Architecture Project
description: Document Added & Updated: 0332CG-AIA- Coburn Gore AIA Questions & Answers V2 Dated 09 September 2026 The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents or Permanent Workers of the United States) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal buildings nationwide. GSA announces an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the new construction of the Coburn Gore Land Port of Entry (LPOE) in Coburn, Maine. The new facility will strengthen supply chains, improve operational capabilities and facility infrastructure, spur economic growth, and bolster the country�s security. The project will provide a fully operational LPOE that coordinates with the tra?c ?ow and operations of the Canadian port of entry at Saint-Augustin-de-Woburn Quebec, Port of Entry. The project will provide a new port that allows Customs and Border Protection to more efficiently carry out its agency mission, their operations and interactions with the public. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $275,000 to $400,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by the SAM Contract Opportunity�s Response Date. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). Instructions on how to submit application materials and join the Registry are available on the following Web site: https://www.gsa.gov/real-estate/design-and-construction/art-in-architecturefine-arts/art-in-architecture-program/art-in-architecture-national-artist-registry All artists who wish to be considered as candidates for a commission at the LPOE in Coburn Gore, ME must have their application materials submitted and received by GSA by 12:00 PM Eastern Time on 22 October 2026. Artists� submissions received after the deadline will not be considered for this project but will be eligible for consideration on future GSA commissions alongside the other artists on the Registry. Artists already on the Registry need not resubmit but may elect to update their information prior to the deadline. GSA evaluates artists based on the following criteria: the media, materials, content and style of the artist�s past work, along with the artist�s past performance and experience with commissions or projects similar to the one described in this synopsis. Shortlisted artists will be contacted and asked to submit additional information, including a statement that the artist can perform the work associated with the GSA commission within the identified budget. GSA will count the combined weight of all the selection criteria as significantly more important than price. At minimum, the scope of services for this commission will require collaboration with the lead designer selected for the land port of entry project; travel to the project site; development and presentation of preliminary and final concepts; fabrication of the artwork; participation in meetings and conservation reviews as necessary; delivery and installation of the artwork; professional documentation of, and detailed maintenance planning for the artwork at the project site. For informational purposes: Artists selected for the contract award must be Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of award. Instructions for creating an account and activating registration in SAM may be found at www.sam.gov. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to renew the registration in SAM on an annual basis for the duration of the project. In accordance with Executive Order (EO) 13934, agencies should prioritize the commission of works of art that portray historically significant Americans or events of American historical significance or illustrate the ideals upon which our Nation was founded. Inquiries concerning the project should be directed to the following email address: Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov and reference the synopsis number in the subject line.

description: PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Project work includes maintenance dredging of Fort Pierce Harbor with excavated material being placed onto Fort Pierce Beach. title: Design-Build Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR) of Equipment Concentration Site (ECS), B-56767, at North Fort Hood, TX
description: *****AMENDMENT 0001 IS ISSUED TO PHASE II SELECTED OFFERORS ONLY ON TUESDAY, 22 SEPTEMBER 2026***** Request for Proposal (RFP), Solicitation No. W912QR25RA013 is issued for the repair of a failing Equipment Concentration Site (ECS), B-56767, at North Fort Hood (formerly Fort Cavazos), TX. This project will repair and construct an addition to an existing ~26,000 square feet of the maintenance part of the Equipment Concentration Site, Maintenance Building 56767, that is in a failing condition, and has not undergone any major infrastructure or system repairs, only limited maintenance and repair work has occurred. The project includes repair of HVAC and Electrical systems, remove non-structural interior walls to right-size rooms and create open flexible workspace, restore inadequate and non-code compliant bathrooms, repair light fixtures with code compliant units, failed flooring, code compliant fire alarm and suppression system, repair electrical conduit distribution throughout the facility. Access for individuals with disabilities will be provided to include a code compliant entrance ramp. The restored facility will meet minimum DOD Antiterrorism standards. This project contains options. The contract duration is estimated at 913 calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed (NTP). This award is Subject to the Availability of Funds (SAF). The technical information contained in each Offeror's proposal will be reviewed, evaluated, and rated by the Government. Phase II Selected Offerors are requested to submit additional information described in Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and evaluation by the Government. The selection process for Phase II will evaluate such factors as: Design Narrative, Management Plan, Schedule Narrative, and Price. All evaluation factors, other than cost or price, are considered approximately equal to cost or price. CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: The estimated construction magnitude is anticipated to be between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. description: DESCRIPTION THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR INVITATION FOR BIDS. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The Norfolk District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, is anticipating a future procurement for a firm-fixed-price construction contract for Maintenance Dredging of the Quinby Creek Federal Navigation Channel located in Accomack County, Virginia. DESCRIPTION OF WORK The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Norfolk District, is seeking qualified and experienced firms capable of performing maintenance dredging of the Quinby Creek Federal Navigation Channel in Accomack County, Virginia. The work consists of dredging approximately 200,000 cubic yards of maintenance material from the Federal channel. Dredging will be performed using a hydraulic cutterhead pipeline dredge, with dredged material hydraulically placed within the Government-designated overboard placement site in Upshur Bay. The maximum contract pay depth will be -7 feet mean lower low water (MLLW). In accordance with FAR 36.204(g), the estimated construction price range for this project is between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The small business size standard applicable to Dredging and Surface Cleanup Activities is $37,000,000. title: Quinby Creek Maintenance Dredging
description: DESCRIPTION THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS, INVITATION FOR BIDS, OR SOLICITATION. NO SPECIFICATIONS OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Norfolk District, is conducting market research for a potential firm-fixed-price construction contract for maintenance dredging of Quinby Creek Channel in Accomack County, Virginia. DESCRIPTION OF WORK The work consists of maintenance dredging approximately 200,000 cubic yards of material from the Quinby Creek Federal navigation channel. Dredging will be performed using a hydraulic cutterhead pipeline dredge, with dredged material hydraulically placed within the designated overboard placement site in Upshur Bay. The maximum contract pay depth will be -7 feet mean lower low water (MLLW). In accordance with FAR 36.204, the estimated magnitude of construction is between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, with a $37,000,000 small business size standard applicable to Dredging and Surface Cleanup Activities. CONSTRUCTION TIME The Contractor will be required to commence work within 15 calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The anticipated period of performance is approximately 180 calendar days from issuance of the NTP. SURVEY OF THE DREDGING INDUSTRY The following survey is intended to assist USACE in assessing the capabilities of prospective dredging contractors and determining the appropriate acquisition strategy. Provide your company name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. Would your firm be interested in bidding on this requirement if a solicitation is issued? If no, briefly explain why. Has your firm performed dredging projects of similar nature, complexity, and magnitude within the past five years? Has your firm managed dredged material placement sites with inflows similar in magnitude to this project within the past five years? If so, provide a brief description of the project(s), customer, contract value, and reference point of contact and telephone number. Would your firm compete as a sole contractor, prime contractor with subcontractor(s), or joint venture? Is there a dollar limit on the size of contract your firm would bid? If so, identify the limit. What is the largest dredging contract, by dollar value, for which your firm served as the prime contractor? What is your firm's bonding capacity per contract and total aggregate bonding capacity? Identify your firm's business size and all applicable socioeconomic categories, including Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, and Women-Owned Small Business. Is your firm familiar with the safety and health requirements of EM 385-1-1? SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS Responses should consist only of a concise narrative addressing the information requested above. Additional information may not be reviewed. This Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. The information received will be used to assist the Government in determining an appropriate acquisition strategy. Prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at SAM.gov to be eligible for contract award. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice must be submitted no later than 22 October 2026 via email to LTC George Jackson and Luke D. Hedlund. Any future solicitation for this requirement will be issued through SAM.gov.

title: Craney Island Rehandling Basin Dredging
description: DESCRIPTION OF WORK The work consists of maintenance dredging, hydraulic placement of dredged material, and debris removal at the Craney Island Rehandling Basin. The project is located on the southeast side of the Craney Island Dredged Material Management Area (CIDMMA), adjacent to the Norfolk Harbor Channel in Portsmouth, Virginia. Maintenance dredging and debris removal will occur in the following areas: � North Access Channel to a depth of -18 feet MLLW � South Access Channel to a depth of -18 feet MLLW � Debris Channel to a depth of -9 feet MLLW � Rehandling Basin to a depth of -20 feet MLLW Optional bid items will include increased dredging depth within the Rehandling Basin to -23 feet MLLW. The estimated quantity for the base work is approximately 260,000 cubic yards of dredged material, including allowable overdepth and anticipated accretion. Debris, including wire, rope, steel, and wood, may be encountered during dredging operations and shall be managed and removed by the Contractor. All dredged material shall be hydraulically transported by pipeline and placed at the Government-furnished upland placement site within the Craney Island Dredged Material Management Area. CONSTRUCTION DURATION The Contractor shall commence performance within 15 calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Proceed (NTP) and complete all work within 180 calendar days. There are no known dredging time-of-year restrictions associated with this project. SURVEY OF THE DREDGING INDUSTRY Interested firms are requested to provide the following information: Company name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. Indicate whether your firm would be interested in submitting a bid for this requirement. If not, briefly explain why. Describe your firm's experience performing dredging projects of similar size, scope, and complexity. Include project descriptions, customers, contract values, dredging quantities, and dredge plant utilized. Identify the type of dredge plant and supporting equipment your firm owns and/or operates that would be suitable for this requirement. Describe your firm's experience managing upland dredged material placement sites with inflow volumes similar to this project. Indicate whether your firm would compete as a prime contractor, as part of a joint venture, or with subcontractors. Provide your firm's bonding capacity, both single-project and aggregate. Identify your firm's business size and all applicable socioeconomic categories, including Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), and Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB). SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Responses shall be limited to a concise narrative addressing the information requested above. Additional information may not be reviewed. This notice is for market research and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. The Government will use the information received to assist in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy, including consideration of potential small business participation. Responses shall be submitted via email to: LTC George Jackson, Contract Specialist george.jackson@usace.army.mil CC: Tiffany N. Kirtsey, Contracting Officer tiffany.n.kirtsey@usace.army.mil Responses are due no later than 22 October 2026 at 2:00 PM Eastern Time. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION Any future solicitation for this requirement will be issued through SAM.gov. All prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to contract award. No attachments or additional documents are provided with this notice.

title: Survival Vest Improvement System
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. The Naval Air Warfare Center, Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Patuxent River, Maryland is requesting information and conducting market research to identify and determine if there are potential sources to manufacture and deliver a Survival Vest Improvement System (SVSI). SVSI is comprised of a new survival vest, VIPER, and a low-profile Life Preserver Unit, Serpent. VIPER is a NAVAIR owned design that incorporates a Small Business Innovative Research (SBIR) armor release system designed by Bunker Supply. The LPU Technical Data Package is owned by Switlik Parachute Company. As part of its market research, NAVAIR - PMA202 is issuing this Sources Sought to determine if there exist an adequate number of qualified interested contractors capable of providing the requirement. The Government may use the responses to this Sources Sought for information and planning purposes. This Sources Sought is only for the purpose of identifying potential sources as part of NAVAIR � PMA202 market research. No Request For Quote (RFQ) exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the RFQ. Responses to this Sources Sought are not quotes on which the NAVAIR � PMA202 can issue any contract. This Sources Sought is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not itself constitute an RFP or RFQ. The Government does not intend to award a contract vehicle based only on responses to this Sources Sought. All information received in response to this Sources Sought marked "Proprietary" will be protected and handled accordingly. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained in their response. Responses to the Sources Sought will not be returned. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Sources Sought. NAVAIR � PMA202 will not pay for information received in response to this Sources Sought. Do not submit pricing information in response to this Sources Sought. Interested sources shall provide a response detailing their capability to manufacture and deliver SVSI. Respondents should provide a brief description of their experience manufacturing similar equipment, including any relevant past performance data (if available). Additionally, respondents should include their experience with manufacturing Critical Safety Items. Respondents should also describe their capacity; production quantities are anticipated between 260 and 1543 annually with the potential to go higher . The Government anticipates a solicitation for a five-year Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) in Fiscal Year 2027. The Government will provide a TDP with the solicitation in FY27 for the vest. The government does not possess or own data rights necessary to distribute for the LPU. Any interested parties MUST copy all parties listed below: Greg Tollefsen, Procurement Contracting Officer gregory.e.tollefsen.civ@us.navy.mil Amy Wescott, Contract Specialist amy.l.wescott.civ@us.navy.mil No telephonic responses WILL NOT be accepted.

title: Nationwide Support to Marine Forces Reserve in Disposing of Hazardous and Nonhazardous Waste and Provision of Environmental Compliance Services
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a request for proposal and no contract will be awarded from this notice. There will not be a solicitation, specifications, or drawings available at this time. This notice is a market research tool used for planning purposes only to determine the availability and capability of businesses. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Mid-Atlantic (NAVFAC MIDLANT) is seeking Large Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, certified HUBZone Small Business, certified 8(a) Businesses with current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel and capability are encouraged to respond. Upon review of industry response to this Sources Sought Notice, the Government will determine whether a set-aside acquisition in lieu of full and open competition is in the best interest of the Government. A Firm-Fixed Price/Indefinite Quantity type, performance-based contract is anticipated. The total contract term including the exercise of any options, shall not exceed 60 months. Source Selection procedures will be used to evaluate and select the proposal that is most advantageous to the Government. The Contractor shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, materials, transportation, and equipment required to perform environmental services and regulated waste collection and disposal at Marine Forces Reserve (MARFORRES) facilities located in 48 states (all states not including Alaska and Hawaii), Puerto Rico and the District of Columbia and at Naval Reserve Centers and Navy installations within the Naval Facilities Engineering Command Mid-Atlantic Area of Responsibility including the following states: Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, and Wisconsin. General Work Requirements: The contractor shall provide environmental services that include, but are not limited to: Coordinate and schedule the collection and disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous, universal waste, potentially infectious medical wastes and sharps, used tires, scrap metal / bulk debris, electronic waste, and other regulated wastes. Provide and manage a customer accessible, web-based system for all disposal record, waste characterization information, disposal facility audits and related data and information. Recycle, to the maximum extent possible, including (but not limited to): used oil, used anti-freeze, batteries and other recyclable materials and universal wastes. Perform on-site waste stream characterization, waste profiling, hazardous and other regulated waste compliance tracking, recordkeeping and reporting. Provide pollution prevention materials (drums, absorbents, spill kits, etc.) and equipment to government facilities. Perform sampling and laboratory analysis of waste materials, building components, drinking water, and environmental conditions in soil, wastewater and surface water. Provide on-site solvent and aqueous parts washer services. Provide oil water separator inspection, cleaning and pump out, maintenance and repair services. Perform petroleum storage tank inspections, cleaning, pump-out, maintenance and repair services. Perform radon facility testing, and maintenance and repair of radon ventilation mitigation systems. Perform maintenance and repair of hazardous material and regulated waste facilities, storage lockers and equipment and associated fire suppression and alarm systems. Perform surveys of facilities for environmental contaminants, including lead paint, asbestos, mercury containing devices, PCB-containing electrical components, mold, low level radiological materials and historical record (EDR) searches. Perform cleanup of environmental contaminant spills. Inspect compressed gas cylinders and determine compliance with DOT hydro-testing, certification and suitability for transportation. Perform lab packing and consolidation and co-mingling of on-site wastes. Perform on-site site waste cleanout activities, including: characterizing and containerizing on-site hazardous materials and regulated wastes, performing sampling and laboratory analysis to determine characteristics and constituents of wastes, packaging and labeling and marking drums, cylinders, and other containers; performing pressure washing and steam cleaning of stained pavements and drains and sewers, pumping out and cleaning storage tanks and lubrication systems and oil water separators. Perform tracking and management of service deliveries, manifests and disposal records; assist in preparation of regulatory required recordkeeping and reporting; tabulate monthly waste and service delivery metrics and costs. Provide oily shop rag recycling / exchange service on a monthly basis. Perform maintenance and installation of storm water management best management practices, including replacement of silt fencing, cleanout sediment from storm inlets, sewers, and structures, and physically remove and dispose of accumulated sediment, debris and vegetation in drainageways. Perform the recovery and disposal of refrigerants from facility HVAC systems and government refrigeration and cooling equipment. Typical regulated waste and hazardous materials managed under this contract includes but not limited to: Used oil; and water contaminated with used oil Waste fuels, gasoline, diesel, heating oil, and others Used antifreeze/coolants and off spec coolants Used oil contaminated absorbents, filters and debris Waste oil and waste oil sludges Used absorbents and rags contaminated with oils and fuels Used lead acid batteries Lithium ion, polymer, metal hydride, manganese and sulfur dioxide batteries Alkaline batteries Waste paint related materials in aerosol cans, caulk tubes, quart, gallon, and larger containers Contaminated coolants - ethylene and propylene glycol (potentially contaminated with water, oil, brake fluid, and fuels) Oily bilge water (>95% water, containing oil, antifreeze, fuel contaminants) - Galveston TX, Gulfport MS, Jacksonville FL, Norfolk VA (Little Creek), Tampa FL, Syracuse, NY and other facilities. Soil and sediments contaminated with fuels, petroleum and lubricants Medical potentially infectious waste, expired vaccines and medications, and used sharps Compressed gas cylinders, empty and containing: inert gases, oxidizers, refrigerants, fire extinguishers, and flammable gases, including over packed leaking cylinders Waste consumer products containing surfactants, oxidizers, corrosives, solvents, and others Corrosive acid and bases Off-specification and expired shelf-life oils, fuels, coolants and other products Used lamps, fluorescent, LED bulbs, aerosol paints, and other universal wastes Lab packing small containers of paint related materials, consumer products, cleaners, and other materials, including labor effort and technician support All Large Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, certified HUBZone Small Business, and certified 8(a) Businesses are encouraged to respond. The Government will not pay for any information solicited. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. All qualified firms are encouraged to respond. The appropriate NAICS Code is 562211. It is requested that interested parties submit a brief capabilities package not to exceed 10 pages. This capabilities package shall address, at a minimum the following: 1. Examples of projects worked within the last five years of similar size, scope and complexity as the work indicated. Knowledge of the Federal and State environmental regulations within the AOR. Indicate whether your firm worked as a prime or subcontractor, contract value, brief description and tabular depiction of how the referenced contract relates to the work

title: Indefinite Delivery Contract for Architect and Engineering (A-E) Services for Surveying and Mapping Services to Support the Jacksonville District and USACE
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement for Indefinite Delivery Contract for Architect and Engineering (A-E) Services for Surveying and Mapping Services to Support the Jacksonville District and USACE. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 541370. There is no solicitation at this time. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. The purpose of this synopsis is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of various members of the Surveying Community to include Small Business Section 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Women-Owned (WOSB), Historically Underutilized (HUBZone) concerns and Other than Small Business Community (unrestricted). The Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of responsible contractors. This scope for AE services will consist of surveying and mapping to support planning, engineering design, construction, operations, and maintenance of civil works projects. Work will include but not be limited to topographic surveying, property/boundary surveys, geodetic control surveys, remote sensing surveys, construction surveys, inland hydrographic surveying, and near-shore hydrographic surveying. The primary purpose of this proposed contract is to provide services for projects located within that portion of the State of Florida that resides in the geographic boundaries of the Jacksonville District area of responsibility. The anticipated contract will be an Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity contract for a period of one year from date of award, with options to extend up to four additional years; not to exceed a total of five years. Any carcass that cannot be repaired must have Defense Contract Mnagement Command (DCMC) Quality Assurance Representative(QAR) approval for disposal. Upon receipt of Government equipment the contractor shall perform incoming inspections, recording any shipping damage, and inventory components for completeness. Units with missing parts will not be inducted until missing partsare received or unless specifically authorized by the Procurment Contracting Officer (PCO). The contractor shall advise the PCO if any portion of the required servicing is a result of the furnishing by the contractor of articles that were defective in material and/or workmanship or otherwise not in conformance with the requirements of the contract under which such government equipment were originally furnished. Repaired Government equipment shall meet the inspection and acceptance test requirements of the applicable repair specifications. A contractor QA representative shall be required, in accordance with MIL-I-45208A, or ISO Quality standard equivalent, to witness repair,inspection, and acceptance tests Government representatives shall be notified of, and permitted to witnesssuch inspections at their discretion. The contractor shall submit repair procedures for Government approval prior to repair if those procedures deviate from the repair procedures detailed in the applicable repair specifications. Where the test specifications are found to be missing,inadequate,or behind in revision for a CLIN,the contractor shall develop and submit its own acceptance test procedures for Government approval to submission of the CLIN for Government acceptance. During the repair effort the contractor shall make no modifications to the CLIN that would prohibit future repair or require additional repair steps by other qualified sources. REPAIR PARTS: The contractor shall be responsible for identification, selection, ordering, and stocking of required piece parts to support all repairs. By definition," piece part" shall be any part or material listed in the applicable repair specification. TEST EQUIPMENT: The contractor will provide a laboratory facility equipped with instrumentation and testing capability for comprehensive functional testing of the equipment and detailed inspections of subassemblies and detailed parts. The contractor test equipment shall be designed to ensure repaired Government equipment function in full compliance with the requirementsof the applicable repair specification. title: Germany – Electricity, heating, solar and nuclear energy – Lieferung von elektrischer Energie Ökostrom für diverse Abnahmestellen von Trägern öffentlicher Verwaltungen im Bundesland Schleswig-Holstein
description: Gegenstand der Ausschreibung ist die Lieferung von elektrischer Energie (100 % Ökostrom) als Vollstromversorgung für die in den Vergabeunterlagen bezeichneten Abnahmestellen der Auftraggeber. Der zur Versorgung der Abnahmestellen gelieferte Strom muss zu 100 % aus erneuerbaren Energien stammen. Ökostrom im Sinne dieser Ausschreibung ist Strom, der aus erneuerbaren Energiequellen erzeugt wird. Zulässige Energiequellen sind insbesondere: Wasserkraft einschließlich Wellen-, Gezeiten-, Salzgradienten- und Strömungsenergie, Windenergie, solare Strahlungsenergie, Geothermie, Biomasse einschließlich Biogas, Deponiegas und Klärgas sowie der biologisch abbaubare Anteil von Abfällen aus Haushalten und Industrie. Soweit Strom aus Biomasse eingesetzt wird, müssen die jeweils geltenden gesetzlichen Anforderungen an die eingesetzten Energieträger sowie, soweit einschlägig, die gesetzlichen Nachhaltigkeitsanforderungen erfüllt sein. Strom aus Kernenergie sowie Strom, der aus fossilen Energieträgern, insbesondere Kohle, Erdgas oder Mineralöl, erzeugt wurde, erfüllt die Anforderungen dieser Ausschreibung nicht. Dies gilt auch für Strom aus Kraft-Wärme-Kopplungsanlagen, soweit dieser unter Einsatz fossiler Energieträger erzeugt wurde. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Die Ausschreibung umfasst insgesamt 2 Lose mit ca. 499 Abnahmestellen und einem jährlichen Gesamtverbrauch von ca. 4,3 GWh. Die Abnahmestellen der Teilnehmer wurden von der ausschreibenden Stelle auf 2 Lose verteilt. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Die tatsächlichen Verbräuche im Lieferzeitraum können nutzungsbedingt von den ermittelten Verbräuchen auf Basis der Verbrauchsdaten im Referenzjahr abweichen. Die Anzahl der Verbrauchseinrichtungen kann ebenfalls während der Vertragslaufzeit variieren. Wegen weiterer Einzelheiten wird auf die Vorbemerkungen zum Stromliefervertrag verwiesen. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Toleranzband: Für das Lieferjahr 2027 gilt für jeden Auftraggeber ein Toleranzband von ± 10 % der für diesen Auftraggeber maßgeblichen Gesamt-Referenzmenge. Die Mindestabnahmemenge zu den vereinbarten Lieferkonditionen beträgt je Auftraggeber 90 % der Gesamt-Referenzmenge des Lieferjahres 2027. Die Maximalabnahmemenge zu den vereinbarten Lieferkonditionen beträgt je Auftraggeber 110 % der Gesamt-Referenzmenge des Lieferjahres 2027. Für die Prüfung des Toleranzbandes werden die tatsächlichen Verbrauchsmengen sämtlicher im Lieferjahr 2027 zur Versorgung angemeldeter Abnahmestellen des jeweiligen Auftraggebers gemeinsam betrachtet. Soweit innerhalb eines Auftraggebers unterschiedliche Preis- oder Messgruppen bestehen, werden deren Verbrauchsmengen für die Prüfung des Toleranzbandes zusammengefasst. Verbrauchsabweichungen innerhalb des Toleranzbandes führen zu keiner gesonderten Mehr- oder Mindermengenabrechnung. Eine gesonderte Mehr- oder Mindermengenabrechnung kann ausschließlich für Verbrauchsmengen erfolgen, die außerhalb des vorstehend festgelegten Toleranzbandes liegen. Hinsichtlich der Einzelheiten der Mehr- und Mindermengenabrechnung wird auf Ziffer 10 dieser Leistungsbeschreibung verwiesen. Die Betrachtung des Toleranzbandes erfolgt für jeden Teilnehmer gesondert. Maßgeblich ist die Summe der tatsächlichen Verbrauchsmengen sämtlicher im Lieferjahr 2027 zur Versorgung angemeldeter Abnahmestellen des jeweiligen Teilnehmers im Verhältnis zu dessen Gesamt-Referenzmenge. Ein Ausgleich von Mehr- oder Minderverbräuchen zwischen verschiedenen Teilnehmern desselben Loses findet nicht statt. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Die maximal beziehbare Energiemenge beträgt für das Lieferjahr 2027 je Auftraggeber 150 % der für diesen Auftraggeber maßgeblichen Gesamt-Referenzmenge. Unabhängig hiervon beträgt die absolute Höchstmenge der im Rahmen des jeweiligen Loses insgesamt beziehbaren Energie 150 % der für das betreffende Los ausgewiesenen Gesamt-Referenzmenge. Der Mengenbereich zwischen 110 % und 150 % der jeweiligen Gesamt-Referenzmenge gehört nicht zum Toleranzband und wird nach den Regelungen zur Mehrmengenabrechnung abgerechnet. Die vorstehenden Höchstmengen stellen keine Abnahmeverpflichtung des Auftraggebers dar. Eine Verpflichtung zur Abnahme besteht ausschließlich nach Maßgabe der Regelungen zum Toleranzband und der sonstigen Vertragsbestimmungen. Mit Erreichen der für das jeweilige Los festgelegten absoluten Höchstmenge können aus der Rahmenvereinbarung keine weiteren Liefermengen zu den Bedingungen dieser Ausschreibung verlangt werden. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Pro Los wird ein Rahmenvertrag mit einem Anbieter geschlossen. Es erfolgt keine Los- oder Zuschlagslimitierung.

title: Submission 211 Baumeister Anbau und Aufstockung AZB, Breitenbach
description:
Gegenstand der Ausschreibung sind die Baumeisterarbeiten im Zusammenhang mit der geplanten Erweiterung und dem Umbau des bestehenden Alterszentrums Breitenbach.

Der Leistungsumfang umfasst sämtliche für die Realisierung des Rohbaus erforderlichen Baumeisterarbeiten. Dazu gehören insbesondere die Baustelleneinrichtung, erforderliche Abbruch- und Rückbauarbeiten, Erd- und Aushubarbeiten, Kanalisations- und Entwässerungsarbeiten, Fundationen, Beton- und Stahlbetonarbeiten, Schalungs- und Bewehrungsarbeiten, Mauerwerksarbeiten sowie ergänzende Arbeiten am bestehenden Gebäude.

Weiter sind die erforderlichen Durchbrüche, Aussparungen, Schlitze, Kernbohrungen und Anpassungsarbeiten im Bestand sowie das fachgerechte Schliessen von Öffnungen und Aussparungen Bestandteil der ausgeschriebenen Leistungen. Ebenfalls enthalten sind sämtliche notwendigen Nebenarbeiten, Transporte, Materialumschläge und Koordinationsleistungen gemäss den Ausschreibungsunterlagen.

Ein wesentlicher Bestandteil des Auftrags sind die Anschlüsse zwischen dem bestehenden Gebäude und der Erweiterung. Die Arbeiten sind entsprechend den Projekt- und Ausführungsunterlagen sowie den geltenden Normen, Vorschriften und behördlichen Vorgaben auszuführen.

Da das Alterszentrum während der Bauzeit weiterhin betrieben wird, sind die Arbeiten etappenweise und unter besonderer Berücksichtigung des laufenden Betriebs auszuführen. Zugänge, Flucht- und Rettungswege sowie die betrieblich notwendigen Erschliessungen sind jederzeit gemäss Bauablauf und Vorgaben der Bauleitung sicherzustellen.

Die Ausführung erfordert eine enge terminliche und technische Koordination mit der Bauleitung sowie mit den übrigen am Bau beteiligten Unternehmern. Die Arbeiten sind gemäss Bauprogramm, Leistungsverzeichnis und den weiteren Bestandteilen der Ausschreibungsunterlagen auszuführen.

Inschrijver dient bij uitvoering te voldoen aan de eisen gesteld in het Programma van Eisen, Bijlage 9. De Broker handelt namens HVC richting de markt. HVC heeft een partij voor ogen die de gehele markt van potentieel aan te bieden Kandidaten kan bestrijken. Het zwaartepunt van onze inhuur ligt bij de afdeling Projecten, die ten behoeve van geheel HVC voornamelijk technische projecten uitvoert, bijvoorbeeld voor onze business unit Warmte, welke zich toelegt op de ontwikkeling en aanleg van voornamelijk warmtenetten en geothermiebronnen. Functies/rollen die veelvuldig worden ingehuurd zijn Plant/Maintenance Engineers, Projectmanagers/-leiders, Werkvoorbereiders en Directievoerders. Daarnaast vindt er enige inhuur van professionals plaats binnen overige bedrijfsonderdelen en ondersteunende diensten, zoals bij HR, Communicatie, Financiën en Juridische zaken. De Broker wordt ten behoeve van HVC verantwoordelijk voor onder andere de volgende processen: - sourcing, preselectie en contracteren van gekwalificeerde Kandidaten door een brede marktontsluiting; - contractmanagement t.a.v. Leveranciersovereenkomsten en Nadere overeenkomsten, screening, leveranciersmanagement, dossiervorming; - urenregistratie en (centrale) facturatie; - (management)rapportages.

description: Upphandlingen omfattar två delar: Bärgningstjänst; flytt av fordon till anvisad uppställningsplatsUppställningsplats; förvaring och skrotning av fordon. UM avser att teckna avtal med en leverantör per delområde, en leverantör kan dock bli aktuell för båda delområden. Anbudsgivaren kan därför lämna anbud på ett eller båda delområdena. Varje delområde utvärderas separat. Ett fordon som är felaktigt uppställt och stör ordning och säkerhet i trafiken och miljön, eller har varit uppställt en längre tid, får i vissa fall flyttas från platsen efter beslut av Trafikverket, Polismyndigheten eller kommunen. I Växjö kommun är det Samhällsbyggnadsförvaltningen som ansvarar för flyttning av fordon. Beslut om flyttning grundas på lagen (SFS 1982:129) och förordningen (SFS 1982:198) om flyttning av fordon i vissa fall. Ett gott samarbete med ömsesidigt förtroende mellan beställare och leverantör är av stor vikt då det gäller hantering av annans egendom. Målet med avtalet är att uppnå en enkelhet i kommunikation och hantering, samt att helhetslösningen blir så kundanpassad som möjligt.

description: The OFFERS DUE DATE is being pushed back to Oct. 22,2026. Currently, RFIs are being answered and additional time is needed. An amendment will be sent out once a response for the RFIs has been completed. Amendment 0001 is to update the solicitation with the following change: 1. Site Visit is scheduled for August 18, 2026, at 1:00 PM Mountain Time. Location: Turner LPOE 41725 Turner Rd Turner, MT 59542 2. RSVP for the site visit by August 13, 2026 to Mark Lovie at mark.lovie@gsa.gov. His cell number is (415)961-0222. Ensure you CC' john.morelion@gsa.gov. 3. RFI's will be due August 26, 2026. 4. Offers will be due September 03, 2026 by 4:30PM MST. All Offer should be emailed to john.morelion@gsa.gov Please be reminded to bring your verification of ID to the site visit. The amendment will be an attachment include a signed copy with your offer. The U.S. General Services Administration intends to solicit construction services for the Turner Roof & Building Envelope Project at the Turner Land Port of Entry, 41725 Turner Road, Turner, Montana 59542, Building No. MT0055AW. The project includes roof replacement and building envelope improvements at the main building, including work on the U.S. and Canadian sides of the facility, and envelope improvements at the water treatment building. Work includes, but is not limited to, selective demolition, roof replacement, exterior wall/cladding repairs, thermal and moisture protection, metals, openings, finishes, and incidental electrical, communications, and securityrelated coordination. The facility will remain occupied and operational during construction. The contractor must phase and secure the work daily, maintain safe access, protect ongoing border operations, and coordinate with GSA, CBP, CBSA, and other stakeholders regarding antennas, cameras, cables, signs, access, security, and inspections. Work affecting the Canadian side may require Canadian access, work permit, and material import coordination.Certain roofing materials may be furnished through the existing roofing warranty process; the contractor will be responsible for coordinating those materials with the manufacturer/certified installer and providing all remaining labor, materials, equipment, supervision, bonds, permits, and incidentals required to complete the work. The contractor shall comply with the solicitation documents, drawings, specifications, applicable codes and standards, GSA PBS Core Building Standards, security and badging requirements, environmental survey requirements, fire/life safety requirements, submittal requirements, and closeout requirements. The anticipated period of performance is 150 calendar days after notice to proceed. The solicitation is expected to include base bid work for the main building roof and envelope on the U.S. side, main building roof and envelope on the Canadian side, and water treatment building envelope work on the U.S. side.

title: Netherlands – Recruitment services – Raamovereenkomst Executive Searchbureaus voor managementvacatures schaal 13 t/m 18
description: Binnen de Provincie Limburg ontstaan jaarlijks enkele vacatures van directie en management, in de schalen 13 tot en met 18, die niet intern of via de Interne arbeidsmarkt kunnen worden ingevuld. Tot nog toe volgt per vacature die we niet intern kunnen invullen een aanbesteding om een searchbureau in te schakelen. Om efficiency redenen is besloten tot een Europese aanbesteding voor het afsluiten van een raamovereenkomst met maximaal drie executive searchbureaus, ter ondersteuning van de werving en selectie procedures voor directie en managementfuncties in schaal 13 t/m 18. We onderscheiden twee percelen, perceel 1 management(directie)-functies in de schalen 15-18: en perceel 2 managementfuncties in de schalen 13-14. Voor elk perceel wenst opdrachtgever maximaal drie bureaus te contracteren. Een opdracht zal pas worden verleend op het moment dat de organisatie er zelf niet in is geslaagd de vacature in te vullen. Provincie Limburg wenst meerjarig samen te gaan werken met per perceel maximaal 3 gespecialiseerde searchbureaus op het gebied van kwalitatief (publiek) leiderschap. Het streven is een meerjarig partnerschip om niet alleen snel en effectief tot invulling van de vacature kunnen komen maar ook kwalitatief doordat deze searchbureaus de organisatie en haar cultuur beter kent (leert kennen) en daardoor beter kan inspelen.

description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), Product Delivery Service PDS) Health Infrastructure and Systems Management (HISM), Clinical Imaging Product Line has a requirement for enhancement of the existing Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) Router Application software that interacts with the VA's Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) Imaging system. DICOM router application software will provide high quality, effective, and efficient Information Technology (IT) services to those responsible for providing care to Veterans at the point-of-care, as well as throughout all the points of the Veterans� health care in an effective and timely manner. DICOM Compass routers are utilized at the operational-level at VA medical centers as well as by the Standards and COTS Integration Platform (SCIP) team, Community Image Exchange Services team, and VA IT Technical Staff to route medical images and studies from Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) Imaging (VI) to other medical diagnostic equipment for analysis and additional processing to improve processing efficiently and fault tolerance by decreasing the overall duty time of each DICOM Compass Router. These routers have key functions that are designed for managing and optimizing the flow of DICOM data within medical imaging environments for data routing, data normalization for DICOM headers ensuring compatibility, optimizing resource utilization through load balancing capabilities distributing across servers/storage solutions to prevent overload, backup/redundancy features ensuring continuous data availability and prevent data loss by duplicating imaging data, workflow management supporting creation of customizable workflows to handle complex scenarios, security/compliance with secure communication protocols protecting patient sensitive data during transmission with audit trail functionality, archival/storage management supporting long-term data retention, integration that ensures seamless flows with various imaging systems (e.g., imaging systems, PACS, electronic health records), and interoperability enhancing functionality between different systems/vendors for a cohesive imaging data management environment. VA facility DCF Run-time licenses are essential component software used by the operations staff at the local VA facilities required to deploy and use LB applications in the production environment. These end user licenses who need to run LB software such as DICOM routers, migrations tools and workflow management capabilities to conduct patient health care services to Veterans.

title: Z2JZ--Upgrade Transitional Residence (TR) House Bathrooms (GI) IFB# 36C26326B0023; PN: 636-24-505 Grand Island VA Medical Center, Grand Island, Nebraska
description: This notice is for informational purposes only and is not a request for submission of bids. THIS IS A TOTAL 100% SERVICE-DISABLED VETERAN OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (SDVOSB) SET-ASIDE. In accordance with Public Law 109-461 and VAAR 819.7003 (b), bidders must be registered and certified as an SDVOSB on the SBA s MySBA Certifications website at https://certifications.sba.gov/ and be able to be verified on the SBA s Small Business Search website at https://search.certifications.sba.gov/. Only bids from verified SDVOSB s at the time of bid submission shall be deemed responsive. All non-responsive bids shall be rejected and ineligible for award. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with the applicable small business size standard of $45 million. In accordance with VAAR 819.7003(b), bidders must represent to the Contracting Officer that it is a small business concern under the NAICS code assigned to this acquisition. In accordance with VAAR 836.204 the magnitude of construction for this project is between $250,000 and $500,000. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Grand Island VA Medical Center, intends to issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) in accordance with the procedures set forth in Part 14 (Sealed Bidding) and 36 (Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts) of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). Network Contracting Office 23 (NCO 23) intends to award a single, firm fixed-price contract for completion of construction Project Number: 636-24-505, Transitional Rehabilitation (TR) House Bathrooms at the Grand Island VA Medical Center located in Grand Island, Nebraska. An IFB Solicitation is planned to be issued on or about August 1, 2026, with an award date within 60 calendar days from bid opening date. Further details of all dates, events, and locations, including site visit and bid due date, will be available in the Solicitation. The Grand Island VA Medical Center currently has a requirement to upgrade nine (9) Veteran Transitional Rehabilitation House (TR) House Bathrooms, with work including a range of demolition/removal, rough/ finish carpentry, plumbing and electrical work. More specifically, work includes but is not limited to demolition/removal of all existing bathroom fixtures/items; installation of all new bathroom fixtures/items, with carpentry, plumbing and wiring, as required. Fixtures and items included, but not limited to, are tubs/showers (including wall bases, surrounds, corner shelves, rods, faucets/valves, shower heads, safety bars, supply lines, etc.); toilets (including seats, flanges, risers, shut off valves, braided supply lines, etc.); vanities (including base cabinets, sinks, faucets, shut off valves, braided supply lines, 3-bulb vanity lights, etc.); vinyl flooring with base trim; wall wainscotting; medicine cabinets with mirrors; towel bars and soap dishes; one (1) each floor to ceiling end wall with metal studs and drywall; including joint compound, primer and paint, as required; and all other associated parts, pieces, hardware and materials required to properly install all the above listed items. The contractor will be required to provide all of the above listed items as well as all other tools, equipment, labor, and supervision necessary to complete the project in accordance with general industry standards, project drawings and the Statement of Work. The Period of Performance (PoP) for this work is one-hundred thirty five days (135) calendar days from issuance of a Notice to Proceed (NTP) and is non-negotiable. A Notice to Proceed date/issuance will be coordinated between VA and Contractor following award. The IFB Solicitation, consisting of various bid documents, specifications, drawings, forms, etc. will be available for download at System for Award Management (SAM) Contract Opportunities (https://sam.gov/content/opportunities). The SAM Contract Opportunities website is the only official location to obtain Solicitation information and documents. These documents will include complete details of the Solicitation and project requirements. Any amendments to the Solicitation will be posted at the same location. Interested bidders are advised that they are responsible for obtaining all bidding documents via Contract Opportunities and for monitoring the Contract Opportunities website for any changes to this announcement and pending Solicitation. No other information regarding scope, dates, etc. is available until issuance of the Solicitation via Contract Opportunities. A bidders list will not be maintained. Hard copies of any documents regarding this project will not be mailed or made available outside of this website. All prospective bidders must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and must be registered and active in the SAM database (http://www.sam.gov). All prospective bidders must complete electronic online Representations and Certifications on SAM. The eventual awardee must also have a current Department of Labor, VETS 4212 Federal Contractor Reporting Filing at https://www.dol.gov/agencies/vets/programs/vets4212 (if applicable).
